title: Limiting reagent and yield; Atom economy; Titrations and solution calculations
source: Questions copied unchanged from the mission-lesson scripts for AQA A-level Chemistry (status of the source: mission-lesson scripts of Oct-Nov 2026 (reviewed by AI reviewers; not signed off by a person)). Terms and clues: AM09#t2 term and clue written for the game; AM10#t1 term and clue written for the game; AM09#t3 term and clue written for the game; AM10#t2 term and clue written for the game. Questions: AM08#N.6a, AM09#N.4a, AM10#N.3, AM08#N.9, AM09#N.6, AM10#N.5, AM08#N.11, AM09#N.10b, AM10#N.9, AM08#N.13, AM08#N.14.

assemble.prompt: Match each term to its definition.

items.label: Excess reactant
items.clue: The starting substance of which some is left over at the end.

items.label: Atom economy
items.clue: Percentage of the total mass of reactants that ends up in the desired product.

items.label: Theoretical yield
items.clue: The maximum mass of product, calculated from the substance that runs out first.

items.label: Addition reaction
items.clue: Gives a single product, so 100% of the starting mass ends up in what is wanted.

questions.stem: Vinegar (ethanoic acid, a weak acid) is in the conical flask. Sodium hydroxide is added from the burette. Which indicator should be used, and what is the colour change at the end point?

options.text: Methyl orange, from red to yellow
Either indicator, because the acid and alkali react in a 1 : 1 ratio
Phenolphthalein, from colourless to pink
Phenolphthalein, from pink to colourless

questions.explanation: Weak acid + strong base: phenolphthalein. It is colourless in the acid and turns pink when a slight excess of alkali is present.

questions.stem: Nitrogen and hydrogen react: N₂(g) + 3H₂(g) → 2NH₃(g). A mixture contains 5.60 g of N₂ and 1.50 g of H₂. Which statement is correct? (Aᵣ: H 1.0, N 14.0)

options.text: H₂ is limiting, because a smaller mass of H₂ is present.
H₂ is limiting, because the equation needs three times as much H₂ as N₂.
H₂ is limiting: 0.750 mol H₂ needs 2.25 mol N₂, and only 0.200 mol N₂ is present.
N₂ is limiting: 0.200 mol N₂ needs 0.600 mol H₂, and 0.750 mol H₂ is present.

questions.explanation: n(N₂) = 5.60 ÷ 28.0 = 0.200 mol; n(H₂) = 1.50 ÷ 2.0 = 0.750 mol. N₂ needs 3 × 0.200 = 0.600 mol H₂, which is available, so N₂ runs out first.

questions.stem: Which statement about atom economy and waste in an industrial process is correct?

options.text: The higher the percentage yield, the higher the atom economy, so less waste is produced.
Atom economy counts one molecule of each substance, so the coefficients do not affect it.
A process with an atom economy of 100% produces no waste of any kind at all.
The lower the atom economy, the greater the proportion of reactant mass that becomes waste.

questions.explanation: The mass not in the desired product ends up in by-products, so atom economy and waste are inversely related.

questions.stem: A student records these titres: 24.30 cm³ (rough), 23.85 cm³, 23.40 cm³ and 23.50 cm³. Which mean titre should be used in the calculation?
questions.explanation: Only 23.40 and 23.50 cm³ are concordant (within 0.10 cm³). Their mean is 23.45 cm³.

questions.stem: Which statement describes the theoretical yield of a product in a reaction?

options.text: The mass of product actually obtained at the end of the experiment
The total mass of all the reactants put in, since mass is conserved
The mass of product calculated from the amount of the limiting reactant
The mass of product calculated from the reactant with the smaller number of moles

questions.explanation: The theoretical yield is the maximum mass of product, from the limiting reactant and the mole ratio, assuming complete reaction and no losses.

questions.stem: Which reaction has an atom economy of 100% for the product named?

options.text: CaCO₃(s) → CaO(s) + CO₂(g), making calcium oxide
H₂SO₄(aq) + 2NaOH(aq) → Na₂SO₄(aq) + 2H₂O(l), making sodium sulfate
2SO₂(g) + O₂(g) → 2SO₃(g), making sulfur trioxide
Any reaction that is carried out with a 100% yield

questions.explanation: This reaction has a single product, so every reactant atom ends up in it: 100%.

questions.stem: Now the mission: vinegar. 10.0 cm³ of vinegar is titrated with 0.500 mol dm⁻³ NaOH, using phenolphthalein. The mean titre is 16.60 cm³. CH₃COOH(aq) + NaOH(aq) → CH₃COONa(aq) + H₂O(l). What is the concentration of ethanoic acid in the vinegar, in mol dm⁻³?
questions.explanation: n(NaOH) = 0.500 × 0.01660 = 8.30 × 10⁻³ mol. Ratio 1 : 1, so 8.30 × 10⁻³ mol of acid. Divide by the vinegar volume, 0.0100: 0.830.

questions.stem: Thermite is a mixture of aluminium and iron(III) oxide. 2Al(s) + Fe₂O₃(s) → Al₂O₃(s) + 2Fe(l). A mixture of 10.0 g of Al and 10.0 g of Fe₂O₃ reacts, and 5.60 g of iron is collected. What is the percentage yield of iron? (Molar masses: Al 27.0, Fe₂O₃ 159.6, Fe 55.8 g mol⁻¹)
questions.explanation: n(Al) = 0.370 mol; n(Fe₂O₃) = 0.0627 mol. Divided by coefficients, 0.185 against 0.0627: Fe₂O₃ limits. n(Fe) = 2 × 0.0627 = 0.125 mol; theoretical 6.99 g. 5.60 ÷ 6.99 × 100 = 80.1%.

questions.stem: Hydrogen is manufactured by reacting methane with steam: CH₄(g) + H₂O(g) → CO(g) + 3H₂(g). In one batch, 16.0 kg of methane gave 4.80 kg of hydrogen. What is the atom economy for producing hydrogen by this reaction? (Aᵣ: H 1.0, C 12.0, O 16.0)
questions.explanation: 3 × 2.0 ÷ (16.0 + 18.0) × 100 = 6.0 ÷ 34.0 × 100 = 17.6%. The products total is the same: 28.0 + 6.0 = 34.0. The rest of the mass ends up as CO.

questions.stem: A student titrates 25.0 cm³ of a weak acid, HA, with 0.100 mol dm⁻³ NaOH. The student then titrates an identical 25.0 cm³ sample of HA to which 50.0 cm³ of distilled water has been added. How does the volume of NaOH needed to reach the equivalence point compare with the first titration, and why?

options.text: It increases, because the flask now holds a larger volume of solution
It is unchanged, because the moles of HA in the flask are unchanged
It decreases, because the HA in the flask is now more dilute
It is unchanged, because adding water does not alter the pH

questions.explanation: Water changes the volume and concentration in the flask, not the moles of HA. The same moles of NaOH, so the same volume, are needed.

questions.stem: Limewater is a solution of calcium hydroxide. Ca(OH)₂(aq) + 2HCl(aq) → CaCl₂(aq) + 2H₂O(l). 25.0 cm³ of limewater is titrated with 0.0500 mol dm⁻³ HCl, using phenolphthalein. The mean titre is 18.40 cm³. What is the concentration of calcium hydroxide, in mol dm⁻³?
questions.explanation: n(HCl) = 0.0500 × 0.01840 = 9.20 × 10⁻⁴ mol. One Ca(OH)₂ reacts with two HCl: n = 4.60 × 10⁻⁴ mol. Divide by the sample volume, 0.0250: 0.0184.
